sentences.text: Thus, the triple test of likelihood of confusion is satisfied in the present case.
15.14.The Plaintiff's products bearing the Subject Mark are Schedule H drugs, which are essentially prescribed by doctors, for treating anemia, inter alia, to women during their pregnancy.
Thus, requisite licenses and permissions have been obtained by the Plaintiff under the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 for manufacturing and marketing the drugs in India.
The Plaintiff's products bearing the Subject Mark are not over-the- counter products but can be prescribed only on a doctor's prescription.
The Defendants have obtained permission under the provisions of the Foods Safety and Standards Act, 2006, which is inter alia applicable to 'food' and 'nutraceuticals'.
Thus, the Impugned Products are over-the-counter products and can be dispensed without a doctor's prescription.

Thus, on account of the Defendants adopting the Impugned Mark and the Impugned Trade Dress, there are chances of confusion between the Plaintiff's products bearing the Subject Mark and the Impugned Products, and there is possibility of harm and injury being caused to patient population, including but not limited to pregnant

15.15.The Defendants have deliberately adopted the Impugned Mark and the Impugned Trade Dress, for marketing identical products, and the same has been done without the Plaintiff's authorization, consent or license, and in violation of the Plaintiff's statutory and common law rights.
15.16.The adoption of the Impugned Mark and the Impugned Trade Dress by the Defendants is dishonest and thus the subsequent user cannot purge the Defendants' conduct.
There is no explanation for the adoption of the Impugned Mark and the Impugned Trade Dress, for trading in identical services, catering to an identical class of customers.

15.17.The Defendants have slavishly and unauthorizedly copied the Plaintiff's artistic work and distinctive design elements in the Subject Trade Dress, and thus, the Defendants have infringed the Plaintiff's copyright in the Subject Trade Dress.
Such acts of imitating or substantially reproducing the Subject Trade Dress by the Defendants constitute infringement of the Plaintiff's copyright.

15.18.The alleged acts of the Defendants in deliberately adopting the Impugned Trade Dress is aimed at misrepresenting to the general public as to the source of the Impugned Products and that the Impugned Products are in some way connected to the Plaintiff, when no such relation exists.
The Plaintiff does not have any control over the quality of the Impugned Products.

sentences.text: Plaintiff in many ways in as much as it completely erodes the distinctiveness which is associated with the Subject Mark and the Subject Trade Dress.
Defendants' subsequent adoption of the Impugned Mark for nearly identical products amounts to infringement of the Subject Mark under Section 29 of the Trade Marks Act, 1999.

The conduct of the Defendants in addition to infringement of the Subject Mark amounts to passing off of the Subject Mark and Subject Trade Dress, copyright infringement, misrepresentation and dilution as well as unfair competition and thus the Defendants are liable to be restrained by an order of this Court.

16. This is a case of triple identity, where the Marks are identical, the products category is identical,
and the trade channels as also the consumer base are identical.
17. The material placed on record shows that the Plaintiff is the prior adopter and continuous user of the Subject Mark and its variants, including the Mark 'OROFER-XT' and the Subject Trade Dress.
The Plaintiff is also the registered proprietor of the Subject Mark and has used the Subject Mark extensively and continuously since 1996.
Prima facie, the Impugned Mark adopted and used by the Defendants is visually, phonetically and structurally similar to the Subject Mark.

To an unwary consumer of average intelligence and imperfect recollection, the Impugned Mark and the Subject Mark are likely to appear identical, leading to confusion and deception as to the source, origin or association of the Impugned Products.
18. The Impugned Trade Dress reproduces the essential and distinctive This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 26/12/2025 at 20:36:00 features of the Subject Trade Dress.

A comparison of the Impugned Trade Dress and the Subject Trade Dress shows a striking similarity in the overall colour combination, layout, placement of the product name and composition, and graphical elements.

The near identical Impugned Mark and the Impugned Trade Dress indicates a deliberate and dishonest adoption by the Defendants, aimed at riding upon the goodwill and reputation of the Subject Mark and the Subject Trade Dress.
19. Having considered the material placed on record and the submissions made by the learned Counsel for the Plaintiff, a prima facie case is made out in favour of the Plaintiff.
The adoption and use of the Impugned Mark and the Impugned Trade Dress for nearly identical products is likely to result in confusion, misrepresentation and deception amongst consumers.
The balance of convenience lies in favour of the Plaintiff, as continued manufacture and sale of the Impugned Products would dilute the distinctiveness of the Subject Mark and Subject Trade Dress.
The Plaintiff is likely to suffer irreparable injury to its goodwill, reputation and statutory rights if interim protection is not granted.

20. Accordingly, till the next date of hearing, the Defendants, their directors, executives, partners,
proprietors, principal officers, assignees, retailers, distributors, wholesalers, family members and anyone acting for and on their behalf are restrained from manufacturing, selling, distributing,
